title: Design principles: hierarchy, redundancy, scalability and documentation

videos.script: Lesson 3 named the shapes a network can take. This lesson is about choosing them on purpose, for a whole campus. {{campus}} Four ideas carry the design. Hierarchy: the devices in tiers, core, distribution and access, each tier with one job. {{tiers}} Redundancy: two of whatever everybody depends on. You will cut a cable between a distribution router and the core while a ping runs, and count what was lost. In this run, nothing. {{redundancy}} Single points of failure: the box that has no twin. You will switch off pc1's gateway and watch pc1 lose everything, while the doubled core sits there unused. {{spof}} Scalability: an address plan that still makes sense at ten times the size. You will count the routes on a core router. {{scale}} And documentation: a cable table and an address table, read straight off the network, so that they are true on the day you need them. {{docs}} The lab is a small campus. Two core routers, two distribution routers, two access switches and two PCs. Small enough to read on one screen, and big enough to break in four different ways. {{lab}}
